newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly molasses report - June 23.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly molasses report - June 23.

text.p: Prices on sugarcane molasses were steady to $5.00 lower per ton in the week ended June 21, USDA Market News said in their weekly National Molasses report.

Molasses supplies are moderate and demand is light. Domestic molasses usage remains light to moderate. Lower prices for corn as well as light demand and grazing pressure pushed molasses prices lower, according to USDA.
Feed Molasses (minimum 79.5 brix, 43% sugars, except where noted) wholesale prices, tank car or truck, fob terminal, prompt delivery, dollars/ton, 1/
Type/Market Area As of Noon: Last Week Last Year

1/ Per ton prices are based on 171 gallons for blackstrap molasses. To compute cents per gallon prices on cane molasses divide dollars per ton by 171 gallons ($ per ton divided by 171 gallons = cents per gallon). Ton - 2,000 lbs; Gallon= U.S. gallon.

**Prices represent sales fob terminal to the general feed trade in the respective areas but do not necessarily reflect sales to other trade areas.** * Includes the major Uppper Mississippi river tributaries with the exception of the Missouri River. Source: USDA-Illinois Dept of Ag Market News Springfield, Il. 217-782-4925.
